result_text:
`all_files.zip` now takes its entry names from the configured scope aspect names, so renaming an aspect no longer breaks the export. I compiled the `reports` module (clean build) but did not run any tests, and I did not try a renamed config end to end.

The change is in `DataExporter.java`, in the zip step near the end of the data export. It used to read five hard-coded filenames, which is why a renamed aspect made the read fail. The `catch (Throwable)` then skipped everything after it, which is why `git-history.zip` went missing too.

It now takes the five scope aspects (main, test, generated, build and deployment, other) and names each entry with `DataExportUtils.getAspectFileListFileName(aspect, "")`. That is the same function that names the loose `aspect_<name>.txt` files, so each lookup matches what was written. The entries keep the same order, so the default config gives the same five names as before. A renamed aspect such as `buildAndDeployment` gives `aspect_buildAndDeployment.txt` in fourth place.

I didn't touch the `aspect_main.txt` and `aspect_build_and_deployment.txt` literals in `LandscapeAnalyzer.java` (lines 280 and 283). They read the exported files by fixed name, so they'd miss a renamed aspect too.
